title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to choose safe and healthy foods to protect the health of both mother and baby. In this article, we will provide information on foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly to avoid health risks.

## Foods to Limit
According to the CDC, NHS, and FDA, there are several types of foods that pregnant women should limit or avoid, including:
- Deli meats and processed meats: These foods can contain Listeria bacteria, which can harm the fetus.
- Unpasteurized dairy products and raw milk: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain E. coli, Salmonella, and Listeria bacteria.
- High-mercury fish: Fish high in mercury, such as shark, swordfish, and king mackerel, can harm fetal development.
- Undercooked and raw foods: Undercooked and raw foods, such as sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs, can contain Salmonella and E. coli bacteria.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
To ensure food safety, pregnant women should cook the following foods thoroughly:
- Meat and poultry: Cook meat and poultry to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure that bacteria are killed.
- Eggs: Cook eggs to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to ensure that bacteria are killed.
- Seafood: Cook seafood to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to ensure that bacteria are killed.

## Practical Tips
To ensure food safety, pregnant women can follow these tips:
- Always check the label to ensure that the product has been pasteurized.
- Cook food to the recommended internal temperature.
- Avoid eating processed and raw foods.
- Wash hands frequently when handling food.

## When to Seek Care
If pregnant women experience any of the following symptoms, they should seek medical attention immediately:
- High fever
- Abdominal pain
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting

faqs.question: Are deli meats safe for pregnant women?
faqs.answer: No, deli meats can contain Listeria bacteria, which can harm the fetus.

faqs.question: Can high-mercury fish affect fetal development?
faqs.answer: Yes, high-mercury fish can harm fetal development.

faqs.question: How can pregnant women ensure food safety?
faqs.answer: Pregnant women can ensure food safety by cooking food to the recommended internal temperature, avoiding processed and raw foods, and washing hands frequently when handling food.
